4.8. Transitioning to YAML-based Configuration#

As of 2025, SUEWS has adopted a new YAML-based format for input files to enhance readability, maintainability, and user experience. To help users migrate their existing table-based input files to this new format, a transition tool is provided.

Forcing files and saved output have their own upgrade notes in Upgrading Across the Units Change.

This guide explains how to use the suews convert command (formerly suews-convert, which still works as a deprecated alias) to automate the conversion process.

suews convert always produces a single YAML file in the current schema. When the input is a legacy table set, the process involves two main steps:

  1. Table Version Update (if needed): If you are using input files from an older version of SUEWS, the tool first converts them to the latest available table-based format.

  2. Conversion to YAML: The tool then reads the complete set of (updated) table-based inputs and converts them into a single, comprehensive YAML file.

The same command also accepts a df_state snapshot (*.csv/*.pkl) or an older YAML configuration (*.yml/*.yaml) and upgrades it to the current schema. Table-to-table conversion between legacy releases is not available from the command line; use supy.util.converter.convert_table() from Python (see Configuration Converter API).

4.8.1. Prerequisites#

Ensure that supy is installed in your Python environment (see Installation). The transition tool is part of the supy package.

4.8.2. Using the Transition Tool#

The suews convert command is installed with the supy package and can be run directly from the command line.

suews convert [OPTIONS]

4.8.2.1. Command-Line Options#

Required arguments:

  • -i, --input FILE: The input file. For a legacy table set this is the RunControl.nml file itself (not its directory). The converter reads the FileInputPath parameter from it to locate the actual table files (e.g., if FileInputPath="./Input/", it looks for tables in the Input/ directory next to RunControl.nml). A *.csv/*.pkl df_state snapshot or a *.yml/*.yaml configuration is also accepted.

  • -o, --output FILE: Path for the output YAML file.

Optional arguments:

  • -f, --from VERSION: The version of your source input (e.g., 2020a, 2024a for tables; a SuPy release tag or schema version for YAML). If not specified, the tool will auto-detect the version.

  • -d, --debug-dir PATH: Directory to save intermediate conversion files for debugging (table and df_state inputs only).

  • --no-profile-validation: Disable automatic profile validation and creation of missing profiles.

  • --format text|json: Report format; json emits the standard SUEWS JSON envelope on stdout.

4.8.3. Examples#

4.8.3.1. Example 1: Auto-detect and Convert to Latest YAML#

The simplest way to convert your files to YAML format - let the tool detect the version automatically:

suews convert \
    -i /path/to/suews_run_london/RunControl.nml \
    -o /path/to/new_config/config.yml

The tool will: 1. Read the given RunControl.nml 2. Auto-detect the version of your input files 3. Find table files using the path specified in FileInputPath (e.g., ./Input/) 4. Convert them to the latest YAML format 5. Create config.yml in the specified output location

4.8.3.2. Example 2: Converting to YAML with an Explicit Source Version#

If you know your source version and want to explicitly specify it:

suews convert \
    -f 2024a \
    -i /path/to/old_runs/london_2024a/RunControl.nml \
    -o /path/to/yaml_configs/london.yml

Note: The converter reads FileInputPath from RunControl.nml to locate the table files.

4.8.3.3. Example 3: Converting Older Tables to YAML#

If you have input files from an older SUEWS version (e.g., 2019b), you can convert them directly to YAML:

suews convert \
    -f 2019b \
    -i /path/to/archive/2019_runs/site_v2019b/RunControl.nml \
    -o /path/to/updated_configs/site_2019.yml

The tool will: 1. Read the given RunControl.nml 2. Find table files (typically in Input/ subdirectory as specified by FileInputPath) 3. Update the tables from 2019b through intermediate versions 4. Convert to YAML format

4.8.3.4. Example 4: Table-to-Table Conversion (Python only)#

Converting between legacy table versions without creating YAML is not a command-line feature. Use convert_table() from Python instead, passing run directories rather than the Input/ tables folder itself:

from supy.util.converter import convert_table

convert_table(
    fromDir="/path/to/suews_run_v2020a",
    toDir="/path/to/suews_run_v2024a",
    fromVer="2020a",
    toVer="2024a",
)

fromDir is the run directory containing RunControl.nml; the source tables are read from the folder its FileInputPath points to. toDir receives the converted RunControl.nml at its root, with the converted tables and namelists in its FileInputPath folder and an empty FileOutputPath folder beside it. Forcing files are not copied, so copy them across yourself. Keep FileInputPath relative: with an absolute path the converter writes the converted tables and namelists into that same folder, replacing the originals. See Configuration Converter API for the full signature.

4.8.3.5. Example 5: Debugging Conversion Issues#

If you encounter issues during conversion, use the debug directory option to inspect intermediate files:

suews convert \
    -f 2016a \
    -i /path/to/legacy_runs/2016a_site/RunControl.nml \
    -o /path/to/yaml_output/site_config.yml \
    -d /tmp/suews_debug

This saves all intermediate conversion steps in the debug directory (/tmp/suews_debug), allowing you to identify where issues occur in the conversion chain.

4.8.3.6. Version Auto-Detection#

The converter can automatically detect the version of your input files by analysing:

  • File naming patterns (e.g., SUEWS_AnthropogenicEmission.txt vs SUEWS_AnthropogenicHeat.txt)

  • Column headers in specific tables

  • Parameters present in RunControl.nml

  • Presence of optional files like SUEWS_SPARTACUS.nml

If auto-detection fails, you’ll be prompted to specify the source version explicitly using the -f option.

4.8.3.7. Path Resolution and File Location#

The converter handles various directory structures by reading the FileInputPath parameter from your RunControl.nml file:

  • Configured paths: The converter respects custom paths specified in RunControl.nml when reading source tables

  • Absolute and parent-relative paths: Used as specified when reading source tables (e.g., /home/user/data/inputs/ or ../shared/Input/). When convert_table() writes converted tables to toDir, any FileInputPath that is absolute or resolves outside toDir (such as a ../ path or an escaping symlink) is rewritten in the output RunControl.nml to a relative folder inside toDir (e.g., ./Input/) so source files are not overwritten. Passing a toDir (different from fromDir) that resolves to the source input directory raises a ValueError before any files are written. FileOutputPath is left unchanged, and an external FileOutputPath directory is not created (only a relative FileOutputPath resolving inside toDir is created). Forcing files are not copied by convert_table; suews convert still locates forcing files using the original RunControl.nml FileInputPath

  • Relative paths: Resolved relative to the directory containing RunControl.nml (e.g., ./Input/ becomes <run_dir>/Input/) and preserved when inside toDir (unless it would overwrite the source input directory or escape toDir via a symlink)

  • Automatic fallback: If files aren’t found at the configured path, the converter automatically checks:

    1. The directory containing RunControl.nml

    2. The path specified in FileInputPath

    3. The Input/ subdirectory

This ensures compatibility with various SUEWS installation structures while respecting user configurations.

4.8.4. Migrating legacy bulk Wuh volumes#

Bulk Wuh is now a site-mean external water-use depth in mm accumulated over each forcing interval. This is a breaking unit change from historical forcing files that supplied bulk Wuh as a volume in m3. Convert each old interval value before running:

\[Wuh_{mm} = 1000 \, \frac{Wuh_{m^3}}{A_{grid,m^2}}\]

where \(A_{grid,m^2}\) is the horizontal plan area of the grid cell. This conversion preserves the grid-total water volume, but it does not preserve the historical allocation between surfaces. The old runtime divided the volume by the total irrigated area and then applied each surface’s irrigation_fraction. Consequently, using only the converted bulk value can change surface stores and evaporation even though the grid-total input is the same.

To reproduce that historical surface allocation, supply all seven wuh_<surface> columns (including explicit zeros) using

\[wuh_i = 1000 \, \frac{Wuh_{m^3}}{A_{grid,m^2} \sum_j (sfr_j \, IrrFrac_j)} \, IrrFrac_i\]

where \(sfr_j\) and \(IrrFrac_j\) are the historical surface fraction and irrigation fraction for surface \(j\). If the denominator is zero, the historical runtime supplied zero observed water use. Supplying every surface column is necessary because an omitted surface otherwise falls back to bulk Wuh.

The wu_mm header remains an alias for Wuh, but aliases do not perform unit conversion. SUEWS deliberately provides no magnitude detection or legacy-unit runtime mode, so copying historical bulk values unchanged will give a different water input. Surface-specific wuh_<surface> columns are also non-negative depths in mm per forcing interval and override bulk Wuh for that surface.

4.8.5. YAML Schema Migrations#

Once your configuration is in YAML, subsequent SUEWS releases may bump the YAML schema — the structure of the file itself. Each bump is backed by a registered migration handler, so suews convert (for combined legacy+schema upgrades) and suews schema migrate (for schema-only upgrades) will move old YAMLs onto the current shape without losing data. Every drop is logged with a human-readable reason so you can reconstruct intent if needed.

To upgrade an older YAML configuration to the current installed schema, run:

suews schema migrate site.yml

Omit --target-version so the migrator targets the current installed schema (writing site.migrated.yml beside the original without modifying it; pass --dry-run first to preview changes). Among CalVer schemas, explicit --target-version values are supported only for 2026.4 (from 2025.12 or 2026.1), 2026.6.dev8 and later (from any older schema), and the current schema. Pinning --target-version to an older schema emits a warning and writes a historical schema file that may fail current validation or engine load; use it only when you deliberately need an archived schema shape. Earlier historical labels such as 2026.1, 2026.5 and 2026.6.dev1 to 2026.6.dev7 have no migration route from older schemas, and configurations cannot be migrated to an older schema. If you need a configuration for an older release without a migration route, use that release’s documentation and sample configuration.

The sections below summarise what users see change between schemas. The authoritative lineage (including release-tag to schema mapping) lives in Version History.

4.8.5.1. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev23#

2026.6.dev23 updates modelled leaf area index (LAI) phenology to use daily growing/senescence degree-day increments within fixed growth and senescence seasons (reset before accumulation on DOY 15 and DOY 196 in the northern hemisphere, swapped in the southern hemisphere), gating leaf-out and leaf-off onset on gdd_base and sdd_base:

  • Retune ``lai_power`` and onset thresholds: coefficients calibrated for the legacy cumulative GDD/SDD formulation (for example growth_gdd: 0.001) will under-drive seasonal canopy growth under the daily-increment equations. Set gdd_base (positive, K d), sdd_base (negative, K d), base_temperature, base_temperature_senescence, and lai_power for the daily-increment formulation (the shipped sample uses base_temperature: 6.5, base_temperature_senescence: 22.0, gdd_base: 120.0, sdd_base: -240.0, and lai_power: (-0.02, 0.04, -1.0, 0.02) while keeping per-surface lai_min / lai_max envelopes).

  • Review initial ``sdd_id``: legacy configurations starting on 1 January with sdd_id: -450.0 begin below sdd_base and will trigger immediate early-January senescence before the DOY 15 winter reset unless reset to 0.0 (matching the updated sample configuration).

  • Ignored legacy compatibility fields: gdd_full, sdd_full, and lai_type remain accepted for compatibility prior to removal, but are ignored by the model kernel.

suews schema migrate preserves existing user values unchanged and logs an advisory for sites using modelled LAI:

suews schema migrate site.yml

4.8.5.2. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev22#

2026.6.dev22 removes the two facet-specific SPARTACUS optical properties from the shared BuildingLayer schema so each lives only on its owning facet model, and aligns their Pydantic defaults with the Rust bridge, sample configuration, and legacy tables:

  • roof_albedo_dir_mult_fact is declared exclusively on RoofLayer (sites[*].properties.vertical_layers.roofs[*], default 1.0).

  • wall_specular_frac is declared exclusively on WallLayer (sites[*].properties.vertical_layers.walls[*], default 0.0).

Both owning fields are non-optional numeric values: explicit null or {value: null} raises Pydantic ValidationError on direct configuration loading and YamlUpgradeError during migration to 2026.6.dev22. Legacy YAML files carrying the ignored cross-facet keys (roofs[*].wall_specular_frac or walls[*].roof_albedo_dir_mult_fact) still load with a DeprecationWarning while stripping the dead cross-facet keys, and suews schema migrate drops them cleanly with an explicit log entry:

suews schema migrate site.yml

4.8.5.3. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev21#

2026.6.dev21 unifies three validation contracts across the configuration pipeline and runtime engine handoff:

  • Land-cover surface fraction sum policy: Phase B, Phase C (including suews validate -p C --dry-run), SUEWSConfig.validate_for_engine(), and SUEWSSimulation.run() now share one three-band sum kernel. Per-site sfr sums within 1e-6 of 1.0 pass, drift between 1e-6 and 1e-4 is reported as a warning and can be auto-normalised on the dominant surface via suews validate --science-fixes apply, and deviations exceeding 1e-4 (or all-zero/non-finite/out-of-range fractions) are rejected. Raw SUEWSConfig loading continues to accept off-sum configurations so callers can inspect or repair them before engine handoff.

  • Blocking half-specified daylight saving: setting only one of anthropogenic_emissions.startdls or enddls is now a blocking Phase B error under --science-fixes suggest and --science-fixes off. Under --science-fixes apply, SUEWS fills only the missing bound when daylight saving applies to the site coordinates while preserving the supplied bound; sites without daylight saving remain a blocking error until the lone bound is removed.

  • Centralised required physics list: all validation phases derive the required top-level and STEBBS physics switches from a single definition in supy.data_model.core.model.

Existing YAML files remain structurally loadable. Upgrading through 2026.6.dev21 preserves surface fractions and daylight-saving values unchanged and logs an advisory for any site with off-sum land-cover fractions or a half-specified daylight-saving window:

suews schema migrate site.yml

4.8.5.4. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev20#

2026.6.dev20 aligns Python TenMinuteProfile (including HeatingSetpointProfile and CoolingSetpointProfile) and Rust apply_day_profile_overrides step-key validation across the five 10-minute STEBBS profiles (building_archetype.profile_metabolism, building_archetype.profile_setpoint_temperature_heating_air, building_archetype.profile_setpoint_temperature_cooling_air, stebbs.profile_flow_hot_water, and stebbs.profile_appliance). Previously, Python coerced arbitrary keys via str(k) (accepting malformed keys such as "+1", "0", "145", True, or 1.0 and silently overwriting canonical collisions such as "1" and "01"), whereas Rust rejected YAML integer keys 1..144 while also accepting "+1" and silently overwriting duplicate slots.

Both layers now accept canonical strings "1"..``”144”, zero-padded ASCII-digit strings (such as ``"01" or "0144"), and plain integers 1..``144``, normalising them to canonical "1"..``”144”`` strings while strictly rejecting malformed keys and canonical collisions. Upgrading through 2026.6.dev20 rewrites valid non-canonical 10-minute profile keys to canonical strings and reports any malformed or colliding keys explicitly:

suews schema migrate site.yml

4.8.5.5. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev19#

2026.6.dev19 aligns WeeklyProfile irrigation fields (sites[].properties.irrigation.daywat and daywatper) with the Sunday-first calendar convention used by legacy SUEWS_Irrigation.txt tables, df_state arrays (0=sunday .. 6=saturday), and the Fortran kernel (#2049). Earlier versions mapped monday to slot 0 and sunday to slot 6, shifting asymmetric weekday irrigation schedules by one day on df_state round-trips and legacy table conversions.

Existing YAML files remain structurally valid. Upgrading through 2026.6.dev19 does not rotate or alter weekday keys automatically, because a YAML edited by hand may already carry the intended weekday names. Instead, migration logs an advisory whenever a site defines an asymmetric daywat or daywatper schedule so users who converted from legacy SUEWS_Irrigation.txt tables under an earlier schema can verify that each weekday holds the intended value:

suews schema migrate site.yml

4.8.5.6. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev18#

When model.physics.storage_heat selects EHC (method 5), 2026.6.dev18 defaults model.physics.ehc_surface_coupling to implicit rather than explicit, solving each facet’s linearised surface energy balance together with backward Euler conduction. Four companion optional controls are added under model.physics: control_ehc_stability (default off), control_ehc_initial_profile (default true), resistance_ehc_indoor_roof (default 0.10 m2 K W-1), and resistance_ehc_indoor_wall (default 0.13 m2 K W-1).

Existing method-5 YAML files that omit ehc_surface_coupling remain valid and now run with implicit coupling. To retain the legacy explicit coupling and boundary treatment, set model.physics.ehc_surface_coupling: explicit (other storage heat methods ignore these fields). To migrate an older configuration to the current installed schema:

suews schema migrate site.yml

See EHC coupling and heat diagnostics for boundary conditions, envelope initialisation, and the seven diagnostics appended in output contract 2.1.0.

4.8.5.7. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev17#

Day-of-year windows for irrigation (sites[].properties.irrigation.ie_start, ie_end) and daylight saving time (sites[].properties.anthropogenic_emissions.startdls, enddls) now require whole integers between 1 and 366, or null / omission when disabled. Earlier versions declared float fields and could silently truncate fractional values or turn invalid native inputs into zero.

Migrating through 2026.6.dev17 normalises exact whole-number floats such as 86.0 to 86 (preserving reference metadata) and leaves null, empty mappings ({}), and reference-only mappings ({ref: ...}) as disabled windows. Fractional values (such as 20.5), explicit 0, booleans, non-finite numbers, and integers outside 1..366 stop migration with the affected site and field path so you can choose the intended calendar day explicitly:

suews schema migrate site.yml --dry-run
suews schema migrate site.yml

4.8.5.8. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev16#

Check the initial senescence degree days (sdd_id, in K d) under sites[].initial_states.evetr, dectr and grass. Earlier SuPy versions could accept .nan, .inf or -.inf and run with an initial zero. Migration now identifies the site and vegetation type for each invalid field. Recover the signed value for that site, vegetation type and start date from its initial-condition or restart record. If the intended initial value is zero, either supply 0 or omit that field. When the initial value is unknown, obtain it before migrating the file.

For example, sites[0] (gridiv=27).initial_states.dectr.sdd_id identifies the deciduous trees on grid 27. A finite scalar or a mapping such as {value: -450, ref: {desc: "archived start state"}} retains its value and reference. This example describes a particular initial condition. Choose the value for your own start date and vegetation. Water has no sdd_id.

Keep a copy of the old input and check the migration before saving it:

suews schema migrate site.yml --dry-run
suews schema migrate site.yml

The second command writes site.migrated.yml beside the original. An invalid value stops both commands. Correct the named field in a working copy and repeat the check. A successful migration preserves omission, explicit zero and signed finite values. To reproduce an earlier run that used a non-finite input, retain its original software version and input alongside any corrected run.

4.8.5.9. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev15#

Schema 2026.6.dev12 covers water routing, schema 2026.6.dev13 removes fresh-run radiation memory (see Radiation memory in the 2026.6.dev13 development schema), and schema 2026.6.dev14 removes the remaining continuation-only initial states (see Continuation-only initial state in the 2026.6.dev14 development schema). Upgrading a dev11, dev12, dev13 or dev14 file to dev15 applies those earlier migrations before the drainage coefficient check. For a non-water land surface with sfr > 0 and drain_eq equal to 1, 2 or 3, both storage_drain_params.drain_coef_1 and storage_drain_params.drain_coef_2 must be supplied as finite numbers. Previously an omitted coefficient silently reached the model as zero and could change runoff and evaporation. A coefficient explicitly set to zero remains valid; its meaning depends on the selected equation.

Loading a configuration and running after an in-memory mutation both check this requirement. Python reports a missing coefficient on the first site’s paved surface as sites[0].properties.land_cover.paved.storage_drain_params.drain_coef_1. The standalone engine identifies the same surface by grid ID, for example sites[gridiv=1].properties.land_cover.paved.storage_drain_params.drain_coef_1. Water and zero-area surfaces can retain an omitted coefficient.

Before execution, every active non-water surface must also provide its storage_drain_params block. Sparse construction, loading, updates, annotation and DataFrame round-trips may retain an omitted block, including when the area is explicitly positive. They do not establish that the configuration can run. An empty mapping or a block containing only reference metadata or nulls also retains that incomplete status. Saving and reloading YAML preserves the reference attached to a null value. Engine YAML/JSON export and execution reject the unresolved block. DataFrame round-trips retain it as missing values. Neither conversion invents zero coefficients.

Declared equations 1–3 with missing coefficients still fail configuration validation. Their errors join the existing diagnostic report so unrelated input defects remain visible and requested annotated YAML is still produced. Native resolved YAML must give sfr for each configured land surface; omission is not evidence of zero area.

drain_eq is an integer field. Whole-number floats such as 3.0 remain accepted; active-surface native input and mutable handoff now reject fractions, including near-integers. Previously native input could pass 3.5 through to Fortran, which truncates it with INT and executes equation 3. This could bypass an exact-selector coefficient check. The loader now reports the selector path before the kernel is called, without rounding or choosing an equation.

This change does not assign scientific meaning to integer selectors outside 1, 2 and 3, or turn 0 into a supported no-drainage option. Their existing transport is retained; a wet run with such a selector is not established as valid. Explicit zero coefficients retain their existing acceptance: for example, a zero exponent in equation 3 gives a constant rate before the existing water availability cap. No new default or sign restriction is introduced. The storage capacity fallback from store_max when store_cap is omitted is unchanged.

With schema dev15 or later installed, upgrade an older versioned file (dev11, dev12, dev13 or dev14, or dev15 on a newer installation) to the installed schema beside its original. For a file named site.yml, confirm that the first command wrote site.migrated.yml, then check the saved configuration:

suews schema migrate site.yml
suews validate -p C --dry-run site.migrated.yml --format json

On a dev15 installation, a file already at 2026.6.dev15 needs no migration (suews schema migrate creates no copy); validate site.yml directly. The validation command checks current water-routing, radiation-memory, continuation-state and drainage requirements (along with any later-schema checks on newer installations). Explicitly selecting an older --schema-version on the validation command checks the saved JSON Schema structure. A missing active runoff fraction, for example, can pass that historical structure check and fail model validation after migration.

Migration preserves supplied coefficients, including legacy storedrainprm input and reference metadata. For a declared equation 1, 2 or 3, a missing or null required coefficient stops migration with its path: supply the input and retry. When the entire block is absent, migration preserves that omission and the structural check above can pass. Before running that site, supply storage_drain_params on each active non-water surface. Otherwise suews run site.migrated.yml reports the missing block’s path. Supplied malformed values remain subject to load-time validation.

4.8.5.10. Runoff from paved and building surfaces in schema 2026.6.dev12#

Check the waterdist blocks under sites[*].properties.land_cover.paved and sites[*].properties.land_cover.bldgs if you use runoff from earlier simulations. Some YAML files retain a zero in the unused to_soilstore column from a legacy routing table. Older versions read this zero in place of to_runoff. A simulation could finish successfully while sending too little water to runoff. Schema 2026.6.dev12 uses the runoff fraction you supplied.

For example, these are three entries from a paved-surface routing block. The other five applicable destinations each receive zero in this example.

to_runoff: 0.98
to_grass: 0.02
to_soilstore: {value: 0.0}  # unused on paved surfaces

The intended split is 98% to runoff and 2% to grass. On a sample day with 11.2 mm of rain, the older reader produced 3.589 mm of grid runoff with all three lines present. Removing only the unused last line gave 8.416 mm. The missing 4.827 mm also appeared as a deficit in the grid water balance. With the corrected reader, both files give 8.416 mm and the balance closes. The size of the difference at another site depends on its surface fractions, drainage and weather.

When you migrate from dev11 to dev12, check the following changes in each non-water surface’s waterdist block. Migration removes an explicit numeric zero from a surface’s route to itself (for example, grass.to_grass), from to_soilstore on paved and bldgs, and from to_runoff on evetr, dectr, grass and bsoil. These rules also apply to wrapped zeros such as {value: 0.0}. A non-zero fraction in any of these destinations causes migration to report the site, surface and field to correct.

Migration keeps all fractions for applicable destinations, including zero. In the paved example above, the migrated file keeps to_runoff: 0.98 and to_grass: 0.02. A paved surface with a genuine zero runoff fraction also keeps that zero. See Within-grid water distribution (waterdist) for the applicable destinations and the rules for zero-area surfaces.

The following commands apply to an installation using schema dev12 or later; each migration brings the file up to the installed schema before validation. Choose the command from the version recorded at the top of your YAML file. Keep the converted copy beside the original so relative forcing paths still point to the same files. Use a fresh output filename when you repeat a conversion, so a file left by an earlier run cannot be mistaken for its result.

The file says schema_version: 2026.6.dev11. The first command upgrades site.yml to the installed schema (including the dev12 water-routing step) and writes site.migrated.yml. Confirm that this new file exists. The migration summary can say Needs review even after writing it. Read the diagnostics and run the second command to check the saved configuration:

suews schema migrate site.yml
suews validate -p C --dry-run site.migrated.yml --format json

The file has no schema version. Some older YAMLs are treated as current when their version cannot be inferred. In that case suews schema migrate can exit successfully without creating a copy. The corrected reader still uses the supplied runoff fraction when it loads the original. Inspect paved and building waterdist blocks for the unused to_soilstore zero. You can check this file directly with suews validate -p C --dry-run site.yml --format json. To create a versioned copy, check the release or schema that produced the file in your run records. For example, if it was written with 2026.6.dev11, use the explicit source version below. The converter writes the current schema of the installed software. Substitute the actual source version if it differs from this example.

suews convert -i site.yml -o site.migrated.yml --from 2026.6.dev11
suews validate -p C --dry-run site.migrated.yml --format json

The file already says schema_version: 2026.6.dev12. On a dev12 installation, suews schema migrate creates no copy because the file is already at the installed schema; validate the original directly:

suews validate -p C --dry-run site.yml --format json

On a newer installation, validating the original directly fails with a schema-version mismatch. Migrate site.yml to the installed schema first, confirm that site.migrated.yml was written, and validate the migrated copy:

suews schema migrate site.yml
suews validate -p C --dry-run site.migrated.yml --format json

On installations newer than dev12, migration to the installed schema can also stop on later-schema checks for radiation memory (dev13), continuation state (dev14), drainage coefficients (dev15), vegetation senescence (dev16) and integer day-of-year windows (dev17).

Check each site and surface named in a validation error. An inapplicable non-zero fraction needs a decision about where that water should go. Within a supplied routing block, all seven applicable fractions must be present and sum to one on a surface with positive area. A surface with zero area can leave destinations unspecified until it becomes active. See the complete routing example and list of destinations.

To reproduce an archived calculation, keep the original YAML, forcing and software version together. Changing the schema label alone cannot restore the old reader. To assess the effect on a study, run the migrated copy with the same forcing and dates and compare daily sums of runoff (RO, mm) for each grid, alongside the water balance.

4.8.5.11. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev11#

Schema 2026.6.dev11 requires soil_depth, soil_store_capacity and saturated_hydraulic_conductivity on every active (sfr > 0) non-water surface (paved, bldgs, evetr, dectr, grass and bsoil) in configurations loaded from YAML or a dict. Leaving any of them out or setting it to null now stops loading with an error naming the site, surface and field, and supplying soil_depth as 0 on an active non-water surface with positive soil_store_capacity is also refused. The Rust bridge enforces the same requirements on resolved engine YAML. Inactive surfaces (sfr == 0) and water are exempt, and soil_depth of 0 remains permitted when soil_store_capacity is 0.

Previously, an omitted or null soil parameter reached the water-balance kernel as 0.0 via the Rust bridge. Run the converter to upgrade an older YAML:

suews convert -i old.yml -o new.yml --from 2026.6.dev10

The migration from 2026.6.dev10 preserves valid supplied soil parameters and reference metadata and leaves inactive (sfr == 0) and water surfaces untouched. When soil_depth is missing, null, or explicitly supplied as 0 on an active non-water surface with positive soil_store_capacity, migration stops without writing an output file and reports each affected site and surface: using 0.0 for soil_depth under positive soil capacity breaks wet-day soil water balance. Supply a positive soil_depth (in mm) for each reported surface and re-run the converter. Other missing or null soil parameters on active non-water surfaces (including soil_depth when soil_store_capacity is 0 or omitted) are written explicitly as 0.0 while preserving reference metadata.

4.8.5.12. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev10#

In a surface’s storage_drain_params, the model now reads the current water storage capacity from store_cap. Earlier versions read store_max even when a different capacity was supplied. For example, with store_max of 0.48 mm and store_cap of 2.0 mm, threshold drainage (drain_eq 1) now uses 2.0 mm. This change can also affect evaporation method 1, storage heat method 3 and the building surface under storage heat method 5 with facets.

Run the converter to update the version recorded in the file:

suews convert -i old.yml -o new.yml --from 2026.6.dev9

The upgrade retains both explicit values, including zero, and their references. If the capacity was omitted, it stays omitted and follows the current maximum. To reproduce an earlier run that used unequal values, start from the configuration with store_cap set to the former store_max value.

4.8.5.13. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev9#

soil_moisture_deficit becomes soil_moisture with modelled (0) and observed (1); method 2 is no longer a current-schema option. For modelled configurations, run:

suews convert -i old.yml -o new.yml --from 2026.6.dev8

Alternatively run suews schema migrate old.yml to upgrade through 2026.6.dev9 to the current installed schema. Inactive legacy observation blocks are removed with a logged reason. Current observation blocks are preserved. A second upgrade is a no-op.

Active legacy observations (method 1 or 2) are converted together with their xsmd forcing, by the same command with --forcing:

suews convert -i old.yml -o new/config.yml \
    --forcing old_forcing.txt --forcing-output new/forcing.txt \
    --manifest new/conversion.json --layer-top 0 --layer-depth <metres> --dry-run

The YAML must first carry soil_field_capacity on every contributing surface (see below), and the observed series must be gap-free; the steps are in Converting observed soil moisture. Without --forcing the upgrade fails before writing an output configuration and prints this command. Historical depth is not assumed to be a layer thickness: it is replaced by --layer-depth (recorded in the manifest) unless --legacy-depth-is-thickness confirms it, in which case its millimetres convert to metres. Density converts from grams to kilograms per corresponding cubic unit (factor 1000). References are retained. The Python API is supy.util.converter.yaml_upgrade.upgrade_soil_observation.

smcap is retired because deficits use the configured model soil store. soil_store_capacity is available water capacity, while the new per-surface soil_field_capacity specifies volumetric water content at field capacity. For each positive-area non-water surface, require \(1000\,\theta_{fc}\,d \ge C\), with depth in metres and capacity in kilograms per square metre. Observation top must be zero and thickness must match every contributing soil depth within an absolute tolerance of one micrometre. Modelled runs require no observation metadata or field capacity.

4.8.5.14. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev8#

Schema 2026.6.dev8 no longer accepts a null initial snow albedo. A configuration with

initial_states:
  snowalb:
    value: null

(or snowalb: null) stops loading with an error naming the field. Leave snowalb out to use its default, 0.5.

Earlier suews validate --science-fixes apply runs wrote that null for a site whose run starts in summer or in the tropics; validation now removes the key instead. The migration from 2026.6.dev7 drops a null snowalb and keeps any value you gave, so such a file loads again after suews convert. This changes the initial albedo from the former effective 0.0 to the documented default 0.5. With no initial snowpack, the model resets albedo to zero and the short sample output is unchanged. With non-zero initial snowpack, albedo evolves from the new starting value: radiation and energy fluxes can change with snow enabled. Snow-albedo output can also change with snow disabled, because the albedo update checks snowpack rather than the snow switch. The separate snow-off behaviour is not repaired by this migration.

The same migration replaces a null vegetation sdd_id or water flowchange with an explicit 0.0, preserving their former effective values. This also repairs vegetation-free files emitted by the older table converter. Non-null values and reference metadata are retained.

4.8.5.15. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev7#

Schema 2026.6.dev7 requires the CO2 point source whenever the emissions method adds it to the CO2 flux: a biogenic CO2 method, 11-16, 21-26, 31-36 or 41-46 under model.physics.emissions. Give 0 for a site without a point source:

sites:
  - properties:
      anthropogenic_emissions:
        co2:
          emission_co2_point_source:
            value: 0.0

A configuration loaded from YAML that leaves it out now stops with an error naming the site. Methods 0 to 6 do not use the point source, because the model discards the CO2 flux they compute, so it stays optional there.

Before this schema a missing point source reached the model as 0. The migration from 2026.6.dev6 writes that 0.0 explicitly wherever the point source is absent or null and keeps any value you gave, so an upgraded configuration produces the same output. Upgrade with suews convert.

4.8.5.16. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev6#

Schema 2026.6.dev6 adds include_provisional under model.control.output. Output groups whose variables may still change between releases (BEERS, EHC, NHood, SPARTACUS and STEBBS) are now written to text or streamed output only when it is true:

model:
  control:
    output:
      groups: [SUEWS, DailyState, BEERS]
      include_provisional: true

Saving such a group emits a warning. A configuration that lists one of these groups without the switch still loads, with a warning, but saving that group stops with an error. For an in-memory run, pass include_provisional=True to save() or save() instead. For streamed output, set the configuration switch before calling run(), because that call writes the files.

The 2026.6.dev5 -> 2026.6.dev6 step leaves content unchanged and does not turn the switch on; add it yourself if you rely on one of these groups. suews convert applies the registered content migrations through to the current schema and stamps the output with that version. Default output groups and non-streaming Parquet output are unchanged.

4.8.5.17. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev5#

Schema 2026.6.dev5 renames the shortwave splitting selector to perez. The previous text selector is no longer accepted when loading a configuration. Use the schema converter to update an older YAML before loading it:

suews convert -i old.yml -o current.yml

The 2026.6.dev4 -> 2026.6.dev5 migration step rewrites the retired text selector in both bare and value-wrapped forms under model.physics.kdown_split_method. It preserves reference metadata and all other settings. Numeric option 3 and its calculations remain unchanged; numeric selections and omitted selectors require no content changes in this step. suews convert then continues through the migration chain and stamps the output with the current schema version. Merely changing the version stamp does not rename the old selector.

The new reindl option (numeric 4) is opt-in and needs no additional inputs. See Direct and diffuse shortwave partitioning for both splitting methods.

4.8.5.18. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev4#

Schema 2026.6.dev4 adds optional shading and space-heating controls under sites[*].properties.stebbs:

  • internal_shading defaults to 0 (off); 1 enables constant shading and 2 enables shading when both temperature and radiation thresholds are met.

  • reduction_factor_shading is the retained fraction of transmitted solar gain. It defaults to 1.0 and must be supplied explicitly for modes 1 and 2.

  • temperature_threshold_shading (degrees Celsius) and radiation_threshold_shading (W m-2) default to 0.0 while inactive and must both be supplied explicitly for mode 2.

  • destination_waste_heat defaults to 0 (indoor air); 1 directs space-heating system losses outdoors.

  • fraction_convective_heating defaults to 1.0 (all useful heating to indoor air). The remainder is split equally between indoor mass and the internal wall; with no opaque wall, indoor mass receives the remainder.

Internal shading is represented using a simplified effective solar-heat-gain multiplier, rather than an explicit thermal and optical model of a blind. When shading is active, the window-transmitted solar gain is multiplied by reduction_factor_shading. The retained gain is applied to the indoor thermal mass and subsequently exchanged with the indoor air and other surfaces through the existing heat-transfer processes.

A value of 1 leaves the gain unchanged, while 0 removes this contribution entirely. The excluded fraction is not separately represented as blind absorption, reflection or heat release into the room. The multiplier should therefore represent the effective reduction in net indoor solar heat gain, rather than the blind’s optical transmittance alone.

Shading does not currently modify the daylight factor used by the electric-lighting control.

Existing YAMLs require no new values. The migration preserves their content and any explicitly supplied controls, updating only the schema marker. These defaults preserve the previous control settings; they do not undo physics corrections in the model code.

Upgrade a 2026.6.dev3 YAML with:

suews schema migrate your_config.yml

4.8.5.19. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev3#

Schema 2026.6.dev3 completes the naming-convention sweep for the sites[*].properties.anthropogenic_emissions.co2 section. The migration renames fourteen YAML keys while preserving their values:

Table 4.8 CO2 parameter renames#

Previous key

Current key

co2pointsource

emission_co2_point_source

ef_umolco2perj

emission_factor_co2_fuel

enef_v_jkm

emission_factor_energy_vehicle

fcef_v_kgkm

emission_factor_co2_vehicle

frfossilfuel_heat

fraction_fossil_fuel_heating

frfossilfuel_nonheat

fraction_fossil_fuel_non_heating

maxfcmetab / minfcmetab

emission_co2_metabolism_max / emission_co2_metabolism_min

maxqfmetab / minqfmetab

emission_heat_metabolism_max / emission_heat_metabolism_min

trafficrate

traffic_rate

trafficunits

type_traffic_rate

traffprof_24hr

profile_traffic_24hr

humactivity_24hr

profile_human_activity_24hr

type_traffic_rate keeps the existing numeric values: 1 selects a per-area traffic rate and 2 selects a per-capita rate. The point-source input is a whole-grid CO2 emission expressed as kg C day-1; the metabolic inputs are per capita. Legacy df_state column names do not change.

Upgrade a 2026.6.dev2 YAML with:

suews schema migrate your_config.yml

4.8.5.20. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev2#

Schema 2026.6.dev2 adds the opt-in model.physics.storage_heat: dyohm_building selector (StorageHeatMethod=8). This method uses DyOHM to determine the building storage heat flux only. Other land-cover surfaces continue to use ordinary OHM, and DyOHM surface temperatures are not passed back to the radiation calculation.

Existing 2026.6.dev1 YAMLs do not need content edits for this step because the new selector is optional. The following command migrates to the current schema and stamps schema_version with that version:

suews schema migrate your_config.yml

4.8.5.21. Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev1#

Schema 2026.6.dev1 is a development schema for the SPARTACUS direct/diffuse benchmark work. It extends the 2026.5 surface with default-backed controls:

  • model.physics.kdown_split_method selects forcing-provided, constant-fraction, or Perez-based direct/diffuse shortwave partitioning. The constant split value is nested with the constant selector, for example:

    model:
  physics:
    kdown_split_method:
      constant:
        sw_dn_direct_frac: 0.45

    This value moved from the per-site sites[*].properties.spartacus.sw_dn_direct_frac location to the model-global model.physics selector. Legacy input is still accepted when the new field is absent: matching per-site values are copied into the model-owned value, while distinct per-site values raise a multiple distinct values error and must be reconciled to one shared value before upgrading.

  • sites[*].properties.spartacus gains forest-column stream and vegetation-region settings: n_stream_lw_forest, n_stream_sw_forest and n_vegetation_region_forest.

  • sites[*].properties.vertical_layers.veg_ext optionally overrides the vegetation extinction coefficient per vertical layer; -999 keeps the LAI-derived behaviour.

Existing 2026.5 YAMLs do not need content edits for this step because all new fields have defaults. The following command migrates to the current schema and stamps schema_version with that version:

suews schema migrate your_config.yml

4.8.5.22. Upgrading to Schema 2026.5#

Schema 2026.5 is the YAML schema shipped with release 2026.6.5. It collapsed the 2026.5.dev1 .. 2026.5.dev14 development cycle into a single released label: in release 2026.6.5, one (2026.4 -> 2026.5) handler applied the union of every dev-cycle delta in order, and current migrations from 2026.4 apply that union on the way to later schemas. Upgrading from 2026.4 (shipped with 2026.4.3) brings the following user-visible changes:

  • Fused field names to snake_case (#1256, Category 1): for example netradiationmethod -> net_radiation_method, soildepth -> soil_depth, baset -> base_temperature, crwmax -> water_holding_capacity_max, and 55 more across the model-physics, surface, LAI, vegetation and snow blocks.

  • ModelPhysics selector renames (#1321): the _method / _model suffixes are dropped and domain abbreviations expanded, giving net_radiation, storage_heat, emissions, stability, water_use, roughness_sublayer, frontal_area_index and surface_conductance.

  • STEBBS YAML fully snake_case (#1334, #1337, #1327): the PascalCase exception is retired (124 renames across building_archetype, stebbs and snow), and the hot-water subsystem is unified under hot_water_* (the opaque dhw_* prefix is dropped). For example WallThickness -> wall_thickness, DHWWaterVolume -> hot_water_volume.

  • Naming-convention reorder (#1392, #1394, #1452): field names are reordered quantity-first (wall_external_thickness -> thickness_wall_outer), the archetype_* namespace prefix is applied to whole-archetype fields (building_name -> archetype_name), and building_type is dropped.

  • ``model.control`` restructure (#1372, #1420): model.control.forcing_file -> model.control.forcing.file and model.control.output_file -> model.control.output (inner path -> dir; the legacy output_file: "name.txt" string form is removed). Per-land-cover lai_<surface> / wuh_<surface> forcing columns are now accepted.

  • STEBBS physics nested (#1456): the flat model.physics STEBBS switches fold under model.physics.stebbs (stebbs.enabled + stebbs.parameters; capacitance, setpoint, same_albedo_* and same_emissivity_* move at their leaf names).

  • ``frontal_area_index`` selector (#1495): reduced to observed / modelled; the provided, use_provided and simple_scheme aliases are retired.

Run the migrator without --target-version to apply these changes and continue through to the current schema (see YAML Schema Migrations for supported explicit targets):

suews schema migrate your_config.yml

For a combined legacy-table-plus-schema upgrade, use suews convert, which runs the table conversion first and then walks the schema chain to the current schema and stamps the output with that version.

The handler logs every field rename and drop via [yaml-upgrade]   renamed 'old' -> 'new' (and a human-readable reason on each drop), so you can audit and reconstruct intent. Legacy spellings continue to load through the Pydantic backward-compat shims under a DeprecationWarning; YAMLs that round-trip through the migrator come out in the new spellings and no longer warn. Bridge DataFrame / Fortran column names are unchanged, so there is no model-output change versus 2026.4.3.

4.8.5.23. Upgrading to Schema 2026.4 (SUEWS 2026.4.3)#

Upgrading from 2026.1 (shipped with 2026.1.28) or earlier applies the following deltas:

  • DeepSoilTemperature → AnnualMeanAirTemperature (rename; user-supplied value preserved, #1240).

  • MinimumVolumeOfDHWinUse and MaximumVolumeOfDHWinUse dropped; DHW volume is no longer bounded in the config (#1242). Any values present in your YAML are discarded with a logged reason.

  • STEBBS setpoint fields split: the scalar HeatingSetpointTemperature and CoolingSetpointTemperature continue to work, but are now gated on model.physics.setpointmethod. When the profile branch is selected, use the new HeatingSetpointTemperatureProfile and CoolingSetpointTemperatureProfile siblings (#1261).

  • New daylight-control and lighting/metabolism fields are available as optional additions — they default to sensible values if absent.

To apply these changes and continue through to the current installed schema, omit --target-version:

suews schema migrate your_config.yml

To stop at the historical 2026.4 schema (for example, to target SUEWS 2026.4.3 from a 2025.12 or 2026.1 file), pass --target-version explicitly:

suews schema migrate your_config.yml --target-version 2026.4

Pinning an older --target-version emits a warning and writes a historical schema file that may fail validation or engine load on newer SUEWS installations (see YAML Schema Migrations for supported explicit targets).

4.8.5.24. Upgrading to Schema 2026.1 (SUEWS 2026.1.28)#

Landed with the STEBBS clean-up (#879). If you are moving from the 2025.12 shape (2025.10.15 or 2025.11.20):

  • Building archetype wall/roof fields: Wallx1 → WallOuterCapFrac and Roofx1 → RoofOuterCapFrac.

  • Initial temperature fields renamed: IndoorAirStartTemperature → InitialIndoorTemperature; OutdoorAirStartTemperature → InitialOutdoorTemperature.

  • DHWVesselEmissivity removed — the vessel emissivity is now derived internally rather than carried in the config.

  • Runtime-state view-factor and temperature slots removed from user YAML (they were never user-tunable; #879 finally cleaned them up).

  • STEBBS hourly profiles added for setpoints, appliance, occupants and hot water (#1038). Existing configs that omit them continue to work; the profiles default to previous scalar behaviour.

To apply these changes together with the later schema updates in one pass, run the migrator without --target-version:

suews schema migrate your_config.yml

If you need a configuration for SUEWS 2026.1.28, use that release’s documentation and sample configuration; suews schema migrate has no route to 2026.1 and cannot migrate configurations to an older schema (see YAML Schema Migrations for supported explicit targets).

4.8.5.25. Preserving Your Values Through Renames#

The rename handlers preserve the user’s value. When both the old and the new key happen to be present in the same YAML (for example if you’ve partially hand-edited), the newer value wins and the stale key is logged and dropped so you can spot the intent conflict.

For a dry-run that shows every rename and drop without writing the upgraded file, pass --dry-run:

suews schema migrate your_config.yml --dry-run

4.8.5.26. Troubleshooting#

Common Issues and Solutions:

  1. “Could not auto-detect version”

    • Ensure you pass the RunControl.nml file with -i and that the tables it points to exist

    • Check that your SUEWS table files are present

    • Specify the source version explicitly with -f

  2. “Missing required files”

    • Verify that all required SUEWS table files are present

    • Check the FileInputPath setting in RunControl.nml

    • Ensure files are in the expected directory structure

  3. “Profile validation errors”

    • The converter automatically creates missing profiles

    • Use --no-profile-validation to skip this step if needed

    • Check that profile IDs in tables match those in SUEWS_Profiles.txt

  4. “Conversion chain failed”

    • Use -d debug_dir to save intermediate files

    • Check the debug directory to identify which conversion step failed

    • Report issues with the specific version transition that failed

4.8.6. Nested Physics Sub-Options#

Three model.physics fields accept a family-tagged nested form alongside the existing flat {value: N} shape:

  • net_radiation — families forcing, narp, spartacus.

  • storage_heat — families observed, ohm, anohm, estm, ehc, dyohm, stebbs, dyohm_building. The estm tag is kept so old files still parse; its option 4 is rejected at validation.

  • emissions — families observed, simple, biogenic_rectangular, biogenic_bellucco_local, biogenic_bellucco_general, biogenic_conductance.

Family-tagged form:

model:
  physics:
    net_radiation:
      spartacus:
        value: 1001

Equivalent flat form — the canonical internal representation, and what SUEWSConfig.to_yaml emits:

model:
  physics:
    net_radiation:
      value: 1001

The family tag is a validation gate. Submitting a code that does not belong to the declared family raises a ValidationError pointing at the correct family. For example, {narp: {value: 1001}} is rejected because 1001 is a spartacus code.

Accept-only widening — no schema version bump. Every previously valid YAML continues to validate and round-trips byte-identically. Writing in the nested form is optional and serves as in-file documentation of intent; YAMLs that round-trip through suews schema migrate or SUEWSConfig.to_yaml are always emitted in the flat form.

The Rust CLI (suews run) accepts the same two shapes via the bridge-side normaliser in src/suews_bridge/src/field_renames.rs.

net_radiation also accepts an orthogonal decomposition of the same numeric codes:

model:
  physics:
    net_radiation:
      scheme: narp
      ldown: air

This is equivalent to net_radiation: {value: 3}. Supported schemes are forcing (no ldown or variant), narp (ldown of observed, cloud, or air; optional variant of standard, surface, or zenith), and spartacus (ldown of observed, cloud, or air). As with the family-tagged form, the orthogonal form is accept-only: round-tripping emits the flat numeric form. Human-readable method aliases beyond this explicit decomposition remain out of scope.

emissions also accepts an orthogonal decomposition of the heat/QF and CO2 axes:

model:
  physics:
    emissions:
      heat: j11
      co2:
        anthropogenic: detailed
        biogenic: conductance

This is equivalent to emissions: {value: 45}. Supported heat values are observed, l11, j11, and l11_updated. When omitted, co2 defaults to no CO2 calculation, so heat: j11 is equivalent to emissions: {value: 2}. Supported co2.anthropogenic values are qf_linked and detailed; supported co2.biogenic values are rectangular, bellucco_local, bellucco_general, and conductance. The legacy Fortran code represents anthropogenic and biogenic CO2 together in the 11-16 / 21-26 / 31-36 / 41-46 families, so the orthogonal form rejects unsupported “CO2-only” combinations rather than assigning misleading semantics. Non-biogenic flat codes 4-6 remain accepted as legacy detailed-heat settings, but their CO2 fluxes are discarded by the driver.

4.8.7. Within-grid water distribution (waterdist)#

In legacy tabular input (SUEWS_WithinGridWaterDist.txt; see SUEWS_WithinGridWaterDist.txt), each surface row carried all nine destination columns, placing explicit zeros on the self-routing diagonal and in the unused terminal column (ToSoilStore on impervious surfaces; ToRunoff on pervious surfaces).

In YAML configurations, each non-water surface under sites[*].properties.land_cover.<surface>.waterdist specifies only its seven applicable destinations: the other six surfaces plus to_runoff for impervious surfaces (paved, bldgs) or to_soilstore for pervious surfaces (evetr, dectr, grass, bsoil). The water surface does not take a waterdist block.

Worked example for an active paved surface routing 98% of drainage to surface runoff and 2% to grass:

sites:
  - name: "ExampleSite"
    properties:
      land_cover:
        paved:
          sfr:
            value: 0.43
          waterdist:
            to_bldgs:
              value: 0.0
            to_dectr:
              value: 0.0
            to_evetr:
              value: 0.0
            to_grass:
              value: 0.02
            to_bsoil:
              value: 0.0
            to_water:
              value: 0.0
            to_runoff:
              value: 0.98

YAML validation enforces three rules:

  1. Active vs. inactive surfaces (``sfr > 0`` vs. ``sfr == 0``): All seven applicable destinations (finite fractions in [0, 1] summing to 1.0) are required only when the surface is active (sfr > 0) and a waterdist block is supplied. Omitting the entire waterdist block applies surface-specific defaults. Inactive surfaces (sfr == 0) may omit applicable destinations (or supply an empty waterdist block).

  2. Inapplicable destinations at YAML or model load: Self-routing (to_<self>), to_soilstore on impervious surfaces, and to_runoff on pervious surfaces should be omitted or set to null. For compatibility with files migrated from legacy nine-column tables, an explicit numeric zero (0, 0.0, -0.0, or {value: 0.0}) in an inapplicable slot is normalised to absent (None) when loading through SUEWSConfig.from_yaml, SUEWSConfig.from_dict, or SUEWSConfig(...) while leaving the applicable routed fractions untouched. For example, adding to_soilstore: {value: 0.0} alongside to_runoff: 0.98 and to_grass: 0.02 above clears to_soilstore to None on load and preserves the exact 0.98 runoff fraction. Any non-zero, boolean, or non-finite value in an inapplicable slot raises ValueError.

  3. Post-load live mutations: After loading, editing a live configuration in place to introduce any inapplicable destination (including paved.waterdist.to_soilstore = RefValue(value=0.0) or paved.waterdist.to_paved = RefValue(value=0.0)) or raising sfr from 0 to > 0 on a surface whose applicable destinations are missing raises ValueError before engine execution. These invariants are re-checked at update_config(), run(), SUEWSConfig.to_df_state, and engine serialisation via SUEWSConfig.validate_for_engine. Valid multi-step in-place edits (for example, shifting 0.02 from to_runoff to to_grass across two assignments so the final sum is 1.0) remain supported.

4.8.8. Forcing and output units#

This page covers YAML configuration only. Forcing contract 2.1.0 (declared rain and water-use rates) and output contract 2.0.0 (water fluxes written as interval-mean rates in kg m-2 s-1, units sidecars and DailyState water totals) change forcing files and saved output instead; see Upgrading Across the Units Change.

4.8.9. Radiation memory in the 2026.6.dev13 development schema#

initial_states.qn_surfs and initial_states.dqndt_surf are no longer fresh-run inputs, including when their values are zero. Radiation memory is formed internally using the existing numerical initialisation and recurrence. No preceding meteorological data are required, and all requested output intervals are retained. Early results may depend on cold-start initialisation; there is no fixed time at which the model declares them fully warmed.

Older signed configurations containing seven numeric zeros in either array are accepted with an explicit removal message. Other values, including nulls and malformed arrays, are rejected rather than silently discarded. Remove these fields if a cold start is intended; use a complete checkpoint if continuation is intended. A configuration or a legacy DFState alone cannot restore the complete state and elapsed clock. Zero DFState placeholders remain supported for legacy fresh-run adapters; nonzero memory entries are rejected.

To write an upgraded configuration to the current installed schema:

suews schema migrate site.yml

Unsigned YAML is treated as current input by the Python loader. For an older unsigned file, use suews convert --from <known-source-version> -i old.yml -o new.yml to migrate it; do not merely relabel its schema version. The native engine expects resolved current input and rejects either field regardless of a version label, so migrate legacy YAML through Python or the CLI before passing it directly to the native engine.

The checkpoint representation is unchanged. Its seven-surface order remains paved, bldg, evetr, dectr, grass, bsoil, water; mean radiation memory uses \(\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}\) and its rate uses \(\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}\,h^{-1}}\).

4.8.10. Continuation-only initial state in the 2026.6.dev14 development schema#

The remaining 17 continuation-only initial_states inputs are no longer fresh-run inputs, including when set to zero or legacy default placeholders:

  • vegetation daily irrigation memories: initial_states.evetr.wu, initial_states.dectr.wu and initial_states.grass.wu (wu_total, wu_auto, wu_manual);

  • timer and atmospheric running diagnostics: dt_since_start, tair_av, tstep_prev, l_mod, ustar, ra_h, rb and rs.

Older signed configurations containing legacy cold-start placeholders (numeric zeros for all fields, tair_av: 273.15, or tstep_prev matching model.control.tstep) are migrated with an explicit removal message. Other supplied values, including nulls and malformed mappings, are rejected rather than silently discarded. Remove these fields if a cold start is intended; use a complete checkpoint if continuation is intended. Legacy DFState adapters retain zero/cold-start placeholders and reject non-placeholder continuation values.

To write an upgraded configuration to the current installed schema:

suews schema migrate site.yml

Unsigned YAML is treated as current input by the Python loader. For an older unsigned file, run suews convert --from <known-source-version> -i old.yml -o new.yml rather than relabelling schema_version. The native engine expects resolved current input and rejects these fields regardless of any version label.

Numerical initialisation and the checkpoint payload format are unchanged.

4.8.11. Omitted Optional Fields in Validator-Updated YAML#

When suews validate writes an updated YAML configuration (such as updated_<name>.yml or updatedA_<name>.yml), omitted optional parameters are now left omitted instead of being padded with speculative null placeholders. Omitted optional parameters continue to be listed in the validation report under REVIEW ADVISED, and missing critical model.physics selectors still receive explicit {value: null} placeholders so required fixes remain visible in the updated file. Existing configurations that already carry explicit null values keep them unchanged, and downstream tools or scripts that previously expected validator output to insert null keys for every unused optional field should rely on the validation report or schema defaults instead.
